Contrast Clues - Part 1

What these questions look like

On the test you will see one sentence with a blank in it. Below it sit four answer choices, and each choice is a whole phrase. Your job is to pick the phrase that best completes the sentence.

How to tackle them

Open each step, then press Continue.

Step 1 - find the signal word

Scan the sentence for a signal word like "although", "despite", or "but".

Step 2 - say what the first part claims

Put the first part into your own words. Ask what it claims is true.

Step 3 - flip it, then read the options

Decide what the opposite would sound like before reading any option. Then pick the choice that goes the other way.

Signal word: "although"

How it works

"Although" travels with "even though" and "though", which all work the same way.

"Although" usually sits at the front of the sentence.

The words right after it make a claim that will be outweighed.

The rest of the sentence, where the blank usually sits, goes the other way.

"Although" can also appear in the middle of the sentence.

Although Mia practiced her speech for weeks, she froze on stage.

Your Turn

Answer correctly to continue.

Signal word: "despite"

How it works

"Despite" works the same way as "in spite of".

"Despite" also usually sits at the front of the sentence.

A thing follows it, not a full statement: "despite the rain."

The rest of the sentence then pushes against that thing.

If "despite" sits right before the blank, the answer itself must be a thing.

Despite the heavy traffic, Malik reached the airport with an hour to spare.

Your Turn

Answer correctly to continue.

Signal word: "but"

How it works

"But" shares its job with "yet".

"But" is the odd one out because it cannot start the sentence.

It sits in the middle and works as the turning point.

Everything before "but" goes one way, and everything after goes the other.

Watch for "not ... but rather ...", which trades one idea for its opposite.

The library was silent downstairs, but the upstairs meeting room buzzed with noise.

Your Turn

Answer correctly to continue.

Watch Out For

  • Do not pick a choice just because it sounds true on its own. Check that it flips the first part.
  • The longest, most detailed choice can look thorough. Extra detail does not make a choice right, so test the flip instead.
  • A choice may repeat a word from the sentence. Matching a word is not the same as matching the meaning.
  • Do not read only the part next to the blank. The signal word usually lives in the first part.

Quick Pattern

Ask yourself: which choice goes the other way from the first part? Decide the flip before you read a single option.
